title: Quasi-compactness and separation of spaces are etale local on the target
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $\{Y_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ be a jointly surjective family of etale maps from schemes. Write $f_i:X\times_YY_i\to Y_i$ for the base changes. A morphism $g:X'\to Y'$ of algebraic spaces is called quasi-compact if for every affine scheme $Z$ and every map $h_Z\to Y'$ the algebraic space $X'\times_{Y'}Z$ is quasi-compact, meaning that it admits a surjective etale map $h_U\to X'\times_{Y'}Z$ from a quasi-compact scheme $U$ [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and separated if its representable diagonal is a closed immersion, meaning that each scheme test is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $f$ is quasi-compact and separated if and only if every $f_i$ is quasi-compact and separated.

source.place: Tags 03KG (lemma-quasi-compact-local), (1) iff (4), and 03KM (lemma-separated-local), (1) iff (5); a family is combined by disjoint union. Quasi-compact algebraic spaces as in spaces-properties.tex Tag 03E3 (definition-quasi-compact).

proof.text: Suppose $f$ is quasi-compact and separated. For every affine scheme $Z\to Y_i$, transitivity of fibre products gives $(X\times_YY_i)\times_{Y_i}Z\cong X\times_YZ$; its quasi-compact atlas is provided by the hypothesis on $f$. Thus each $f_i$ is quasi-compact. The diagonal of $f_i$ is the pullback of $\Delta_f:X\to X\times_YX$ along $Y_i\times_Y(X\times_YX)\to X\times_YX$. On every scheme test, this is a scheme base change of a closed immersion; [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] makes it a closed immersion. Hence each $f_i$ is separated as well.

source.place: Tags 03KG (lemma-quasi-compact-local), (1) implies (2), and 03KM (lemma-separated-local), (1) implies (2); scheme base change of closed immersions: morphisms.tex Tag 01QR.

proof.text: Conversely suppose all $f_i$ are separated. Set $B=X\times_YX$. Its base change $B\times_YY_i$ identifies with $(X\times_YY_i)\times_{Y_i}(X\times_YY_i)$; under this identification $\Delta_f\times_YY_i$ is $\Delta_{f_i}$. Thus every scheme test of each base-changed diagonal is a closed immersion. Apply [lem-trf-space-closed-immersion-cover-descent] with $E=X$, $a=\Delta_f$ and $b:B\to Y$. The diagonal is representable by the algebraic-space condition, and the prescribed family covers $Y$, so all hypotheses hold. Its conclusion is exactly that $f$ is separated.

source.place: Tag 03KM (lemma-separated-local), proof of (5) implies (1); its representable descent input spaces.tex Tag 03KD is implemented here testwise by topologies.tex Tag 022C and descent.tex Tag 02L6.

proof.text: Assume now that every $f_i$ is quasi-compact, and fix an affine scheme $Z\to Y$. Set $A=X\times_YZ$. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], the fibre products $Z_i=Z\times_YY_i$ are schemes and $(Z_i\to Z)_i$ is a jointly surjective etale family. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-affine-refinement] to this family over the affine scheme $Z$. It gives finitely many affine opens $W_a\subseteq Z_{i(a)}$ with $(W_a\to Z)_a$ etale and jointly surjective. Each $W_a$ has a map to $Y_{i(a)}$ through $Z_{i(a)}$. Quasi-compactness of $f_{i(a)}$, tested on this affine $W_a$, supplies a quasi-compact scheme $U_a$ and a surjective etale atlas $U_a\to (X\times_YY_{i(a)})\times_{Y_{i(a)}}W_a\cong A\times_ZW_a$. In particular every $U_a$ now has its required map to $A$.

source.place: Tag 03KG (lemma-quasi-compact-local), affine-test reduction and the finite-refinement argument; topologies.tex Tag 0218 (lemma-etale-affine), spaces-properties.tex Tag 03E3 (definition-quasi-compact).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-space-finite-qc-atlas-assembly] to the scheme $Z$, its finite etale covering $(W_a\to Z)_a$, the algebraic space $A=X\times_YZ$, and the quasi-compact scheme atlases $U_a\to A\times_ZW_a$ obtained above. All these maps are over $Z$ by their fibre-product definitions. It gives a quasi-compact scheme $U=\coprod_aU_a$ and a representable surjective etale map $h_U\to A$. This is the required atlas for the arbitrary affine test $Z\to Y$, so $f$ is quasi-compact. Combining this with step 2 gives the converse conjunction, and step 1 supplies the forward implication.
